description: The Coldwater Regional hangar: a cavernous prefab of corrugated steel, its floor a map of old oil stains and tyre scuffs. Tool racks and a battered workbench line one wall; a wheeled ops desk with a bank of flight monitors faces the other. The big bay doors stand open to the west, framing the ramp and the aircraft parked out on it. Beyond the apron a taxiway peels off and runs dead-straight to a long runway — a broad grey ribbon stretched to the horizon, its dashed centreline dwindling to a pale seam, threshold numbers shimmering in the heat off the tarmac, a lone windsock snapping at the far end. It smells of avgas, hot metal and cold coffee.

flags.intro_lore: Coldwater Regional keeps its runway going for the same stubborn reason the whole city does anything: because stopping is worse. The tool racks, the ops desk, the coffee nobody remembers brewing — all of it holds the shape of a working airfield long after the airline it served stopped existing. Somebody still tops off the avgas. Nobody's asked who pays for it.

name: Coldwater Regional Hangar
